argument: Recomputation before verdict. Two rungs of this card print a derived second figure: the middle rung pairs six with two, the top rung pairs eight with four. Halving each parent gives three and four, so only the middle pair was one point short; the top pair already obeyed the rule as printed. The merged text now reads three on the middle line, which is the value my round-one arithmetic asked for, so the filing describes a line the manuscript no longer carries and should stop blocking this topic. Two supporting claims of my own fail under the same recomputation and I withdraw them rather than let them ride: the retired-row story my filing leaned on was never the operative test, because the corrected three is no live row's value either and the opener's instruction to round a halved figure down is what actually governs; and demanding one constant proportion between the two derived figures imported a rule this chapter never states, since each figure is halved from its own parent, which is why three and four are the correct pair and my old rising-by-a-third comparison measured nothing. What survives from my filing is the single point of cold on an Adept card, carried by a different finding on this topic, which I deliberately leave un-rebutted. Class: MECHANICAL, closed by the merge.
